mof_ops.detail: No switch, buyback or T-bill auction in the windows (15-29 Jun). June plan (29 May): one switch auction on 3 Jun (settled 8 Jun; part-1 window, other agent) and no T-bill auctions. MoF wholesale DB shows no operations between 4 and 30 Jun other than the 17 and 24 Jun sales; the T-bill DB has no rows between 8 May and 10 Jul.

In-window June sales incl. additional: 17 Jun 12,791.53m + 24 Jun 13,316.3m = 26,107.83m (both at the 12bn maximum; the offers raised the plan's 6bn minimum to 7bn). Financing of 2026 gross borrowing needs (record PLN 688bn): ~58% after 17 Jun (Erste 18 Jun 08:35) / ~59% (Millennium 18 Jun 08:44) -> ~62% after 24 Jun (MoF to PAP Biznes, Skrot 24 Jun 17:02; Millennium 25 Jun). July/Q3 supply plan: NOT published by 29 Jun - PAP weekly 29 Jun 06:31: 'MF i BGK - podaz obligacji na III kw. i na lipiec' on Tue 30 Jun 15:00 (gov.pl list dates both the July supply and the Q3 financing plan 30.06.2026) - not used. Retail bonds: MoF (Skrot 24 Jun 17:02) keeps July coupons and margins unchanged.

MoF estimate (gov.pl; PAP Skrot 15 Jun 17:06): central budget deficit after May PLN 108,214.2m. PKO 16 Jun: 39.8% of the annual limit, practically the same as after May 2025; May revenue -0.7% y/y (excise -15% y/y on the CPN package, VAT +2.5%, CIT +30%), expenditure +2.7% (FUS transfers +6%); debt service fell y/y in May (timing) but +30% YTD; 'under control'. Erste 16 Jun: 108.3bn a year earlier; May VAT 1.8% y/y, excise 2.7%, CIT 19.0%; no big risk to the 271.7bn plan (the two banks' May tax growth rates differ - recorded as published).

NIK (analysis of 2025 budget execution and monetary-policy guidelines): the MPC's conditional communication in 2025 gave market participants limited information on future policy parameters.

MPC's Kotecki: rate changes unlikely to end-2026, hike appetite lower, too early to signal cuts. Fuel excise back from 15 Jun; VAT 8% and price caps to 30 Jun; Szlapka: gradual exit. MoF offers 7-12bn on 17 Jun (incl. DS1030, IZ0836). SPW rallied on the US-Iran deal: DS0436 5.45% (5.57% Fri).

Tusk: fuel-VAT decision soon; Motyka: conditions to end price caps met (Brent ~$80). BGK: first FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys FPC0427). NBP FSR: the rising SPW share in bank balance sheets adds geopolitical sensitivity. NIK: MPC 2025 guidance gave limited information. PKO: SPW -5-10bp, 2Y/10Y at mid-April lows; DS0436 5.41%.

PS0731 4.44bn at 4.918%, DS0436 2.40bn at 5.416%, OK0129 1.93bn at 4.399%, DS1030 1.09bn at 4.711%. NBP's Sobon: no policy cycle. NIK: the 2025 SRW limit was overstated by PLN 84.5bn; the Fiscal Council wants faster consolidation. ING: MPC more dovish than priced; 10Y ~5.4%, a 3-month low; DS0436 5.40%.
digest.2026-06-19: 18 Jun: MPC's Duda: stable rates the base case, little room for cuts. May voting record: Tyrowicz's +100bp motion rejected again. GUS: June consumer confidence up (BWUK -9.9); price expectations 20.2 from 24.7. BGK switch: sold FPC 1.35bn, bought back FPC0427 1.44bn. Banks: 2026 needs 58-59% financed. After the hawkish Fed (dots) SPW rose 5-7bp (PAP); DS0436 5.44%.
digest.2026-06-22: 19-21 Jun: May industry +4.1% y/y (PAP consensus 2.5%), -0.8% m/m (-2.2%). The Sejm passed the windfall tax (60% rate); it now goes to the Senate. Poland filed its 8th KPO payment request. KSF-M: no regulatory WIBOR replacement needed; no new WIBOR deals from 2027; CCyB 2%. NBP: 12-month FX debt repayments EUR 7.2bn. digest.2026-06-23: 22 Jun: May data below consensus: retail +3.0% y/y (3.8%), wages +5.8% (6.0%), construction +3.9% (4.9%), PPI +2.4% (2.5%); employment -0.9%. mpc.gist: Context only (recapped in PKO/Erste 15 Jun): a cut is now more likely than a hike; members much more optimistic on inflation than a month earlier; a small chance of one small cut this year.

Small probability of rate changes to end-2026, maybe to Q1 2027 when base effects lower CPI; propensity to hike a bit lower than a month ago (not the base case anyway); too early to signal a return to cuts.
Audit office: the MPC's conditional, data-dependent guidance in 2025 gave market participants limited information on future policy.
The NBP neither runs nor announces a policy cycle; it adjusts policy to incoming data under uncertainty, like the Fed and ECB; reserve remuneration at the reference rate is neutral.
